questions.question: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. P ) achieve success Q ) when you R ) and polite S ) stay humble
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

P) achieve success

Q) when you

R) and polite

S) stay humble
questions.solution:
stay humble and polite and polite achieve success
S starts the sentence with "stay humble," setting the foundation of the statement. It gives the first action or advice.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Leisure activities are activities that people ___________ in during their free time while they are not working.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Leisure activities are activities that people ___________ in during their free time while they are not working.
questions.solution: Engage' is the correct choice because "engage in" means to actively participate in or do an activity. The sentence is about what people do during their free time, making "engage" contextually and grammatically correct. 'Exempt' means to free someone from an obligation or responsibility, which doesn’t align with the context as the sentence discusses participating in activities, not avoiding them. 'Evaluate' means to assess or judge something, which is irrelevant because the sentence focuses on engaging in leisure activities, not assessing them.'Encourage' means to motivate or inspire, but the sentence does not imply motivating others to participate in leisure activities.

questions.question: In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative. Mary is the quieter student of the class
questions.questionHtml:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

Mary is the quieter student of the class
questions.solution: quietest" should replace "quieter." In the sentence, "quieter" is incorrect because it is in the comparative degree, which is used for comparing two entities. However, the sentence compares Mary with the entire class, requiring the superlative degree of the adjective.

questions.question: The following sentence contains an error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error. The robbers stabbed him by a sharp knife and he started bleeding profusely on the spot.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence contains an error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error.

The robbers stabbed him by a sharp knife and he started bleeding profusely on the spot.

options.html: but he started bleeding
profusely from the spot
The robbers stabbed her
with a sharp knife

questions.solution: 'with a sharp knife' will be used instead of 'by a sharp knife' because the preposition 'with' is used for instruments or means, whereas 'by' is used for the agent (doer of the action); Like— He was hit with a stick (instrument). The letter was sent by him (agent).

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. How long / have you / been learn / English now?
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

How long / have you / been learn / English now?
questions.solution: 'been learning' will be used instead of 'been learn' because in Continuous Tense, the verb must always be in its Present Participle (V1+ing) form. Hence, the correct sentence will be: "How long have you been learning English now?"
